problem: Existing VLN models are trained offline and stay fixed at deployment. Naively applying online test-time adaptation (TTA) fails because a VLN agent takes many action steps per instruction and executes many instructions in sequence. Frequent updates cause drift, error accumulation and forgetting, while re-initialising per sample discards experience.
motivation: Deployed agents execute instructions online in varied environments and face distribution shift, but there are no labels and supervised or domain-adaptation training is impractical. The paper observes that TTA (Tent) with too-frequent or too-rare updates gives little gain (adaptability-stability dilemma), so update granularity needs to be handled at both the step level and the sample level.
key_idea: Alternate fast updates that use SVD-based gradient decomposition-accumulation over recent steps with slow updates that use SVD-based parameter decomposition-accumulation over historical model states, to balance adaptability and stability in online VLN.
insight: Noisy per-step entropy gradients can be denoised by down-weighting high-variance principal directions (weight 1/λ), and a slow update along the principal axes of the parameter trajectory stabilises long-term drift. In the ablation on REVERIE val-unseen with DUET, SR goes from 46.98 to 48.60 (Tent), 49.74 (fast), 49.82 (+DLR) and 54.15 (+slow), so the slow phase gives the largest jump. Forgetting tests show that a model adapted on unseen data performs on par with the base model on seen data, and stays effective when seen and unseen data are mixed.
method: Setup: an online, unsupervised TTA of a base VLN model (DUET, HM3D-style pretrained DUET, BEVBert, WS-MGMap). Only the last 4 LayerNorm layers (768-d) are updated, using an entropy-minimisation loss on the node action probabilities at each step.

Fast gradient decomposition-accumulation: every M=3 steps, collect the per-step gradients, take the SVD of their covariance, and project the mean gradient onto the eigenvectors weighted by 1/λ. This suppresses high-variance, inconsistent directions. The result is rescaled to the norm of the mean gradient.

Dynamic learning-rate scaling: the trace of the gradient covariance σ_j is compared with a running historical average σ̄ (momentum 0.95). The LR is scaled by Trunc(1+τ-|σ_j-σ̄|) into [0.9,1.1], with τ=0.7 and base LR 6e-4.

Slow parameter decomposition-accumulation: every N=4 samples, collect the final fast-phase parameter states plus the previous slow state and take the SVD of the parameter-variation covariance. Reverting to the historical state gives the reference direction h_l, an exponentially weighted (q=0.1) sum of parameter deviations from the previous slow state.

Slow update: the gradient is Σ_d ε_d·||h||/||ε|| · sign(<h,z_d>) z_d, i.e. the principal axes oriented along h and weighted by eigenvalue. It is applied with a fixed LR of 1e-3, and the result is used for later samples.
Online protocol: batch size 1, test samples shuffled and fed sequentially, 5 shuffled runs averaged.

setting.backbone: DUET (dual-scale graph transformer), HM3D-pretrained DUET, BEVBert, WS-MGMap as base models; test-time updates to the last 4 LayerNorm layers
setting.training_data: Base models are pretrained as in the original works; FSTTA uses only unlabeled test samples online (no extra training data)
setting.observation: panoramic RGB (36 views) with image and object features; graph/topological map; BEV/grid maps for the CE models
setting.action_space: discrete navigable nodes in a topological graph (plus STOP); for R2R-CE, waypoint/graph-based actions of the base models

numbers.extra: online TTA, average of 5 shuffled runs
numbers.evidence: Table tta / reverie / ablation: DUET-FSTTA Val Unseen

numbers_note: Also reported: R2R-CE WS-MGMap-FSTTA (val-unseen SR 40, SPL 35; test-unseen SR 37, SPL 28) and R2R test results were not reported. R2R and R2R-CE numbers are printed as integers.
results: FSTTA lifts DUET on REVERIE val-unseen from SR 46.98 to 54.15 and SPL 33.73 to 36.41, and beats SAR (SR 48.00, SPL 33.92) at lower run-time cost (135.61 ms vs 145.53 ms). It gives gains for DUET, HM3D, BEVBert and WS-MGMap on REVERIE, R2R, SOON and R2R-CE, e.g. HM3D-FSTTA reaches SOON val-unseen SR 42.44 / SPL 31.03 versus GridMM 37.46 / 24.81. On R2R-CE test-unseen, BEVBert-FSTTA has SR 60, matching BEVBert's 59 or slightly improving it.
limitations: Only the last few LayerNorm layers are adapted, so the method assumes normalisation layers exist; it also adds compute and slightly longer trajectories (TL).
The online setting is simulated by shuffling test sets sequentially; there is no realistic online dataset or real robot.
Fast and slow update intervals (M=3, N=4) are fixed and periodic, not adaptive; gains on some metrics are small or mixed.
